summary:
Q1. The lane's X1 statement matches Menon, arXiv:2608.15873v1 (submitted 2026-08-16), Theorem 4.2. Menon states it 'for every group G'. His §2 reduces arbitrary G to a finite core quotient explicitly. No abelian assumption is made, and his own examples are A5 and C2×S4. G-harmonic means only that the cosets are pairwise disjoint: no cover is required and the subgroups need not be distinct. Menon's proof combines Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6 (finite G by the convention of their §3) with his Prop 4.1, a product-set containment argument. The case r1=1 was already published as Margolis–Schnabel Prop 4.7 (Beitr. Algebra Geom. 2019; arXiv v1 2018). [INFERENCE] Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6 Claim 1 says alpha(1,2)=2 in every harmonic X1 tuple. Applying it to a configuration and to its inverse, with the coupling alpha+alpha*≤gcd=3, gives X1 in two lines; the parent should check this. So X1, and the K5.3 exclusion through the deletion bridge, are already known. The lane's contribution is a different proof that does not use Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6.

Q2. My bounded 2026 search found no Sun(k) claim for general groups at k≥5, apart from Gong's unread k=5 thesis claim (dated 2009 in Sun's slides, 2010 on MathOverflow). The 2026 items found were Z-only (Fornal–Sun), length-5 families (Menon), coset partitions only (Garonzi–Margolis; Akman–Sissokho), or covers (Sambale). I found no earlier equivalent of K7-M0, K7-M1, K7-Z2, K7-35, K63-U0, K63-D, K63-E, K63-CLIQUE or K62-A, within the bounded search. These are not deletion corollaries of Sun(t) for t≤6: every pair in K7 has gcd 6, and short subtuples such as (6^5), (6^6) and (3,6^4) can be realised. In Z or a cyclic group the K7 class is trivially impossible (pigeonhole mod 6), so cyclic or Z results cannot settle these cases. Partial overlap: Margolis–Schnabel Cor 3.9 (n=6) and Prop 3.8 exclude only the alpha=1-star subpatterns of K7 and K6.3 [INFERENCE from matching hypotheses]. Every lane partial depends on Sun(5) and Sun(6), which are internally accepted and computer-assisted but unpublished.

Q3. The methods are elementary extensions of standard tools: Margolis–Schnabel §3 and lemmas of Zhu and Menon. The alpha notation is Margolis–Schnabel Notation 3.3. The double-coset measure alpha*/g follows from their Lemma 3.4(1), via |UxV|=|U(xVx^-1)|. The coupling alpha+alpha*≤g then follows from their Lemma 3.2(3); it was already the old-round VFC bound q≤g−alpha, and the only new step is identifying q with alpha*. TG is the three-subgroup version of the pair granularity in Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 3.4(2), which is the lane's old rule P. TG also uses the containment U(V∩W)⊆UV∩UW, as in Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 3.7, 3.10 and Prop 3.8, and Menon Prop 4.1; Zhu's inequality (3.1), r_ijk≤r_ij·r_ik, is related. The singleton case of LFC is Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 3.5; the integer analogue is O'Bryant Lemma 5 (after Huhn–Megyesi). Restricting to one fibre and invoking a smaller case appears in Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6 Claim 1 and in Zhu's proofs. The sources read do not contain the fractional weighting over all fibres or the systematic use of the inverted configuration. Both repackage standard tools and should not be presented as a new method.

Status. A parent verdict now exists (2026-10-19T02:39:50-0700). It accepts K62-A, TG and the corrected full-clique K63-CLIQUE as scoped partials, which supersedes the 'under review' premise of this assignment. K63-CLIQUE is narrow: K6.3 only, with alpha=alpha*=3 on all 15 C–C pairs. It says nothing about K7.

findings.claim: Menon claims the exact X1 family is impossible in every group
findings.quote: Theorem 4.2. Let r₁,...,r₅ be pairwise coprime positive integers with r₁ and r₂ odd. Then, for every group G, the tuple (3r₁,3r₂,6r₃,6r₄,6r₅) is not G-harmonic.
findings.source: M. Menon, Two Questions on G-harmonic Tuples
findings.date_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-08-16 (PDF dated August 18, 2026); /abs/2608.15873v2 returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-19
findings.kind: preprint theorem (not known to be refereed)
findings.verified: statement and proof read in the primary full text (PDF text extraction)
findings.scope: Every group G; five pairwise disjoint left cosets; positive r_i, pairwise coprime; r1 and r2 odd. Identical to the lane's X1 statement.
findings.read_scope: full v1 text, §§1–6 and appendix; the ancillary file verify-counterexample.g was not opened

findings.claim: Menon's 'G-harmonic' requires only pairwise disjoint cosets: no cover, and subgroups need not be distinct
findings.quote: An n-tuple of positive integers (a₁,...,a_n) is called G-harmonic if there exist subgroups U_i ≤ G of index a_i and elements g_i ∈ G such that the cosets g₁U₁,...,g_nU_n are pairwise disjoint
findings.scope: matches the lane's five disjoint left cosets of finite-index subgroups

findings.claim: Menon reduces arbitrary G to a finite group explicitly; non-abelian groups are allowed
findings.quote: Thus any putative example in an arbitrary group has a finite quotient with exactly the same relevant data. Henceforth, G is finite.
findings.kind: reduction lemma (the same core-intersection argument as the lane's R0)
findings.scope: arbitrary group mapped to a finite quotient by the intersection of the cores of the U_i

findings.claim: Menon Theorem 4.2 depends on Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6 and extends Margolis–Schnabel Prop 4.7 (the case r1=1)
findings.quote: Theorem 4.2 strengthens [6, Proposition 4.7], which treated only the case r₁ = 1 ... This does rely on Lemma 1.1, a nontrivial result of Margolis and Schnabel
findings.scope: The known proof imports Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6, which the institute had not accepted as an import. The lane's written proof avoids it.

findings.claim: Menon Prop 4.1 is a product-set containment argument over a triple intersection, the pair-level ancestor of TG
findings.quote: Because U₄ ∩ U₅ ⊆ U₄, we have U₃(U₄ ∩ U₅) ⊆ U₃U₄ ... But U₄ ∩ U₅ ⊆ U₅ gives U₃(U₄ ∩ U₅) ⊆ U₃U₅
findings.scope: Three subgroups of index 6r_j with alpha values (3,1,1). |U3(U4∩U5)| is computed from [G:U3∩U4∩U5], whose multiple of 18r3r4r5 comes from the lcm of the pairwise intersection indices.

findings.claim: Menon mentions coset inversion only as a convention for the GAP check, not as a constraint
findings.quote: Equivalently one may test the right cosets Hg⁻¹: inversion x ↦ x⁻¹ is a disjointness-preserving bijection carrying one family to the other.
findings.scope: The inversion bijection is stated there, but the paper never uses the coupling alpha+alpha*≤g

findings.claim: Provenance context for Menon Theorem 4.2 (not a mathematical premise)
findings.quote: The proof that the Lemma 1.1 configuration is realised in no group (Theorem 4.2) was obtained by Z.ai's GLM-5.2, likewise under prompting.
findings.scope: Bears on review status only. The public priority claim still stands.

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel define G-harmonic for arbitrary G by pairwise disjoint cosets
findings.quote: An n-tuple of positive integers (a₁,...,a_n) is called G-harmonic if there exist subgroups U₁, ..., U_n of G and g₁,...,g_n ∈ G such that the cosets g₁U₁, ..., g_nU_n have pairwise trivial intersection
findings.source: L. Margolis, O. Schnabel, The Herzog–Schönheim Conjecture for small groups and harmonic subgroups, Definition 1.1
findings.date_version: arXiv v1 2018-03-09 (PDF dated November 9, 2018); published Beitr. Algebra Geom. 60 (2019) 399–418, online 2018-10-04
findings.scope: pairwise disjoint cosets; no cover requirement
findings.read_scope: §§1–4 of arXiv v1 via PDF text extraction

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel's lemmas are stated for finite G; their propositions say 'for any group G'
findings.quote: G will always denote a finite group. Whenever we will speak of a group we will mean a finite group.
findings.scope: Lemma 4.6 is stated for finite G. The passage to arbitrary G is the standard finite-core reduction, made explicit in Menon §2.

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6 fixes the alpha pattern of any harmonic X1 tuple
findings.quote: If the 5-tuple (U₁, U₂, U₃, U₄, U₅) is harmonic, then up to permutations between 1 and 2 and permutations between 3, 4 and 5 the following holds.
findings.verified: statement and most of the proof read; part of page 14 garbled in extraction
findings.scope: Indices 3r1, 3r2, 6r3, 6r4, 6r5; r_i pairwise coprime; r1, r2 odd. These are exactly the lane's X1 hypotheses.
findings.read_scope: Lemma 4.6 statement, Claims 1–4 and the eight-case analysis

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel Claim 1 forces alpha(1,2)=2. Combined with inversion, this immediately excludes X1 [INFERENCE]
findings.quote: Claim 1: α(1, 2) = 2 and α(1, j) = α(2, j) for 3 ≤ j ≤ 5.
findings.verified: Claim read in primary. The two-line consequence is my own inference, not stated in any source.
findings.scope: The inverted configuration has the same indices, so alpha*(1,2)=2 as well. The coupling then gives 2+2≤gcd(3r1,3r2)=3, which is impossible. The lane's X1 Steps 2–4 reprove 'alpha(d1,d2)=1 is impossible', which is Claim 1, by another route.

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel left the Lemma 4.6 configuration open; Menon and the lane close it
findings.quote: We are not aware of any group satisfying the subgroup configuration described in Lemma 4.6. Such a group would provide a counterexample to Question 1.
findings.scope: Suggests that Margolis–Schnabel did not use the inversion coupling. This is not evidence that the coupling is new more generally.

findings.claim: The r1=1 subfamily of X1 is in a refereed publication from 2018/2019
findings.quote: Let r₂,..., r₅ be pairwise coprime integers and assume also that r₂ is odd. Then, for any group G, the 5-tuple (3, 3r₂, 6r₃, 6r₄, 6r₅) is not G-harmonic.
findings.date_version: arXiv v1; published BAG 2019 (published text not read)
findings.scope: X1 with r1=1; the proof also uses Lemma 4.6

findings.claim: The lane's alpha is the same as Margolis–Schnabel's alpha
findings.quote: We will denote by α(U, V) the integer satisfying [G : U ∩ V] = lcm([G : U], [G : V])α(U, V).
findings.scope: the same as the lane's alpha_ij = I_ij/lcm(n_i, n_j)

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel already give the double-coset granularity and the conjugate-intersection size formula that TG and INV use
findings.quote: (2) V U ∩ W U consists of double cosets of (V ∩ W)U. Proof. The first statement follows from |U xV | = |U (xV x−1)|.
findings.verified: read in primary; the formula in part (1) is partly garbled in extraction
findings.scope: Pair version (V∩W) of TG's triple intersection. Part (1) gives the double-coset measure alpha(U, xVx^-1)/gcd, which underlies alpha*.

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 3.5 is the singleton-packing ancestor of LFC and of the lane's rule K
findings.quote: Let U₁, ..., U_n, V be subgroups of G such that |U₁V|+... + |U_nV| ≥ |G|. If V U_i ⊆ U_jU_i for any j > i, then (U₁, ..., U_n, V) is not harmonic.
findings.scope: Projection counting in which each fibre holds at most one piece

findings.claim: Margolis–Schnabel Cor 3.9 (n=6) already excludes K7 configurations with an alpha=1 star
findings.quote: [G : U_i] = nr_i and [G : V] = nr, where r₁,..., r_n, r are pairwise coprime. Assume further that α(U_i, V) = 1 for any 1 ≤ i ≤ n. Then (U₁, ..., U_n, V) is not harmonic.
findings.verified: Read in primary. The application to K7, and of Prop 3.8 to K6.3 (a_d=3 divides 6, r_d odd, 5/6+1/3≥1), is my inference.
findings.scope: partial overlap with alpha=1-star subpatterns only

findings.claim: Triple intersection of product sets was already used by Margolis–Schnabel
findings.quote: So considering U₁U₂, U₁U₃ and U₁U₄ as subsets of G and using Lemma 3.1 we obtain ... = 0. A contradiction, since clearly this intersection contains U₁.
findings.source: Margolis–Schnabel, proof of Prop 4.3 (also Prop 4.5 and Lemma 4.6)
findings.scope: Multiway intersection of U_vU_j sets with a lower bound from containing U_v. TG strengthens that lower bound to 1/gcd(n_v,T).

findings.claim: Restricting cosets to one fibre and applying a smaller case inside a subgroup (the LFC(c) step) appears in Margolis–Schnabel
findings.quote: So U₁ ∩ U₃, U₁ ∩ U₄ and U₁ ∩ U₅ are subgroups of U₁ with pairwise trivially intersecting cosets h−1g₃(U₁ ∩ U₃), h−1g₄(U₁ ∩ U₄) and h−1g₅(U₁ ∩ U₅).
findings.scope: One fibre, then Prop 4.2 inside U1. Not a weighted sum over all fibres.

findings.claim: Status in Margolis–Schnabel: Sun's conjecture holds for n≤4 in all groups and n≤20 in Z
findings.quote: This has been confirmed by W.-J. Zhu for n ≤ 4 [Zhu08] for any group G. It has also been proved for G = Z if n ≤ 20 [O'B07].
findings.scope: no k≥5 general-group result cited

findings.claim: Zhu proves Sun's conjecture for k=3,4 in arbitrary groups
findings.quote: Let a₁G₁,..., a_kG_k (k ∈ {3, 4}) be pairwise disjoint left cosets in a group G with [G : G_i]<∞ for all i = 1,..., k. Then ([G : G_i], [G : G_j]) ≥ k for some 1 ≤ i < j ≤ k.
findings.source: W.-J. Zhu, On Sun's conjecture concerning disjoint cosets, Theorem 1.1
findings.verified: read in primary arXiv full text; extraction of pages 5–6 incomplete
findings.scope: k=3,4 only

findings.claim: Zhu has a triple-intersection index bound and coset-counting lemmas that predate the triangle rule T and LFC(b)
findings.quote: HK contains exactly [H : H ∩ K] left cosets of K. ... r_ijk ≤ r_ij r_ik. (3.1) ... (3.1) is useful and it was suggested by Prof. Zhi-Wei Sun.
findings.source: Zhu Lemma 2.1(ii) and inequality (3.1); also the bijection Lemma 3.2 and an inclusion–exclusion count over coset triples
findings.scope: Zhu's r_ij is the lane's alpha_ij and r_ijk is the triple-index ratio

findings.claim: Sun's 2006 statement of the conjecture; at that time it was open even for Z
findings.quote: The case k = 2 will be handled in Remark 2.2. The conjecture remains open even for the additive cyclic group Z.
findings.source: Z.-W. Sun, Finite covers of groups by cosets or subgroups, Conjecture 1.2 and Remark 1.5(a)
findings.scope: Arbitrary groups, finite indices, pairwise disjoint left cosets. Remark 1.5(b) covers p-groups.

findings.claim: Sun's MathOverflow status note: k=5 by Gong (thesis), no progress since 2010
findings.quote: In 2010, Zhu Gong (another student of Nanjing University whose bachelor thesis was supervised by me) confirmed the conjecture for k=5 (again with G a general group). Since 2010, there is no further progress on the conjecture.
findings.date_version: asked 2018-12-02; last edited 2026-01-05 (API timestamp 1767633695); 0 answers on 2026-10-19
findings.kind: status statement by the conjecture's author
findings.verified: read the question body, comments and answers via the StackExchange API
findings.scope: Status statement only; predates Menon 2026; the Gong thesis is unread
findings.read_scope: full question, one comment (pointer to the Herzog–Schönheim literature), no answers

findings.claim: Sun's 2024 talk slides date Gong's k=5 result to 2009
findings.quote: W.-J. Zhu [Int. J. Mod. Math. 3(2008)] proved the conjecture for k = 3, 4 via several sophisticated lemmas. In 2009, Z. Gong confirmed the conjecture in the case k = 5.
findings.source: Sun, talk slides 'Covers of the Integers by Residue Classes and their Extensions to Groups'
findings.scope: The date conflicts with MathOverflow (2010). The 2018 slides (CoverGroupCoset.pdf) mention only k=3,4 and Z k≤20.

findings.claim: The latest 2026 work on the conjecture found is Z-only and recaps group status as k=2, 3, 4 and p-groups
findings.quote: O'Bryant proved the integer conjecture for k ≤ 20 [11]. Zhu proved the group-theoretic conjecture for k = 3,4 [13]. Sun proved the cases k = 2 and the case in which G is a finite p-group [12].
findings.source: J. Fornal, Y.-C. Sun, On the problem of large gcd for disjoint residue classes
findings.scope: G=Z, asymptotic bound; does not cover arbitrary G

findings.claim: The integer case is settled for k≤20, which makes cyclic results irrelevant as kills for the lane's arbitrary-group subclasses
findings.quote: Sun has conjectured that if k congruence classes are disjoint, then necessarily two of the moduli have greatest common divisor at least as large as k. We prove this conjecture for k ≤ 20.
findings.source: K. O'Bryant, On Z.-W. Sun's disjoint congruence classes conjecture
findings.scope: Z only. Its Lemma 5 (after Huhn–Megyesi) is an integer projection-counting analogue of LFC's singleton case.

findings.claim: Garonzi–Margolis is about Herzog–Schönheim partitions, not the gcd conjecture
findings.quote: We prove this conjecture for simple groups and for symmetric groups.
findings.scope: Partitions; method is the arithmetic bound J(G)<2; no disjoint-coset gcd claim

findings.claim: Sambale 2026 is about unions and covers, not the gcd conjecture
findings.quote: Moreover, every subgroup occurring in an irredundant cover of an arbitrary group by n cosets has index at most 2^{n-1}.
findings.source: B. Sambale, On the complement of a union of cosets
findings.scope: covers

findings.claim: A 2026 citer of Margolis–Schnabel treats Steiner coset partitions with commuting subgroups, not Sun(k)
findings.quote: In previous work, we completely classified such groups for up to r=4 mutually commuting subgroups. In this paper, we extend the classification to r=5 mutually commuting subgroups.
findings.source: F. Akman, P. A. Sissokho, Steiner coset partitions for five mutually commuting subgroups
findings.scope: partitions; mutually commuting subgroups; r≤5

findings.claim: Bounded arXiv search: no group-theoretic Sun(k≥5) claim after Menon
findings.quote: Showing 1–4 of 4 results for all: "disjoint cosets"
findings.source: arXiv search; also 'coset partition' (13 hits), 'Herzog-Schönheim' (11), 'harmonic tuple cosets' (1), 'disjoint residue classes' (2), Ginosar (results page 1 of 65), author 'Menon, Murali' (1)
findings.scope: Title/abstract search, not full text. Newest relevant hit is 2608.15873. math.GR, math.CO and math.NT new listings for 2026-10-19 showed no relevant entry.

counterpoints: The K7 and K6.3 partials are not one-line corollaries. Deletion to Sun(t), t≤6, gives nothing, so each proof needs LFC inside U_v together with inversion, parity or LP case analysis.

Margolis–Schnabel left the Lemma 4.6 configuration open, and Menon closed it by another route. This suggests the inversion coupling was not used in those two papers, but it is weak evidence about the wider literature and does not establish that the coupling is new.

The lane's X1 proof avoids Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6. Menon's proof depends on it and on an AI-produced proof step (GLM-5.2), and the preprint is not known to be refereed. The lane's proof therefore independently corroborates the known claim; it does not create priority.
If an external peer-reviewed Sun(5) or Sun(6) appeared, the partials' dependence would shift. If the internal Sun(5)/Sun(6) failed, every LFC-based partial would need re-examination.
Results about Z or cyclic groups (O'Bryant, Fornal–Sun) make every lane class trivial in that setting. They cannot be used to downgrade or to strengthen the general-group results.
open_questions: Parent check of the [INFERENCE] that Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 4.6 Claim 1 plus alpha+alpha*≤3 immediately gives X1. If confirmed, cite it as the shortest known-literature route.
Does the published Springer version (BAG 60 (2019) 399–418) keep the numbering and content of Lemma 4.6, Prop 4.7 and Cor 3.9? Menon cites arXiv page 15, which suggests it does.
Gong's k=5 thesis (2009 or 2010): was a general-group proof ever published, and does it use fibre or packing lemmas like LFC?

Do Huhn–Megyesi (1982), Sun (Chinese Ann. Math. 1992), Berger–Felzenbaum–Fraenkel (1987/88), Korec (1974) or Ginosar–Schnabel (2011) contain a weighted fibre count or an inversion coupling? These were not read.

Do the 'Transversal coset partitions of groups' (2024) or 'Steiner Coset Partitions of Groups' (2025) papers, which cite Margolis–Schnabel, contain multiway-intersection lemmas like TG? Only their titles were seen.
unverified_or_dropped: Gong's k=5 claim: known only from Sun's testimony (MathOverflow says 2010, the 2024 slides say 2009); the thesis was not located.
Menon's ancillary GAP file verify-counterexample.g was not opened; it is irrelevant to Theorem 4.2.
My statements that Margolis–Schnabel Cor 3.9 and Prop 3.8 cover the alpha=1-star subpatterns of K7 and K6.3 are my own hypothesis matching, not stated in any source.

My statement that subtuples such as (6^5), (6^6) and (3,6^4) are realisable rests on elementary constructions (cosets of one index-6 subgroup; Z residues) that I did not run or check against a source.

OpenAlex citer lists were read as titles only (Sun 2006: 14 citers; Zhu: 1; Margolis–Schnabel: 7; Menon: 0). These were dropped as non-relevant by title or abstract: 'Covering by Centralizers' (2026), 'Perpetual Scheduling Under Frequency Constraints' (2025), the 2022 IJMNTA paper, the Chouraqui free-group papers.
Berger–Felzenbaum–Fraenkel, Canad. Math. Bull. 29 (1986), was read in full and dropped: its product-set and parallelepiped method for nilpotent groups is unrelated to LFC, INV or TG.
source_access_limits: arXiv PDFs were read through automatic text extraction. Margolis–Schnabel page 14 is incomplete; the formula in their Lemma 3.4(1) is garbled; a '≠' was lost in their Lemma 4.4. Zhu pages 5–6 are incomplete. Menon's displayed alpha matrix for Lemma 1.1 is garbled, but the statement was cross-read in Margolis–Schnabel.
The Springer version of Margolis–Schnabel is paywalled; only its metadata, abstract and reference list were read. Zhu's journal version (IJMM 2008) was not read; arXiv v1 was.
Sun 2006 was read through Remark 2.2 only (about 330 of 453 extracted lines). Fornal–Sun: pages 1–10 only. Garonzi–Margolis: pages 1–9 of 21. Sambale and Akman–Sissokho: abstracts only.
arXiv search covers titles and abstracts, not full text. Only page 1 of the Ginosar results (25 of 65) was scanned. The math.GR, math.CO and math.NT 'new' listings were checked only for 2026-10-19.
Not attempted: Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, CNKI and other Chinese databases, MathSciNet or zbMATH reviews. No contact with authors, no paid sources.
This was a bounded search. Finding no equivalent does not establish novelty.
